description: The availability capacity heatmap is an interactive map from ESB Networks, the distribution system operator in Ireland, that shows available transformer capacity for new demand and generation at its substations. It covers all 3-phase LV, MV and HV DSO substations: HV substations are grouped by connection voltage (110 kV, 38 kV or MV), and all 3-phase MV/LV substations show available demand capacity for connections below 500 kVA. A demand view and a generation view use colour-coded pins with filters by voltage and capacity range. A downloadable workbook, the July 2026 customer heatmap download of about 7 MB, was last modified on 2 September 2026. The Distribution Network Development Plan page adds demand and generation capacity headroom workbooks for 2025 and a ten-year plan of reinforcement projects under EU Directive 2019/944. Coverage is the ESB Networks distribution system in the Republic of Ireland. The map and workbooks are accessible from the ESB Networks website at no cost under its website terms. Caveats: ESB Networks states the map is a snapshot of transformer capacity only, not upstream capacity, and cannot be relied on alone to judge a connection. Simulation uses are hosting capacity screening for data centres, heat pumps, EV charging and renewables and distribution planning studies. Related records: data-northern-ireland-demand-flexibility-map covers Northern Ireland.
